desc: Ideation and reduction to shortest-common-supersequence of two color chains; verified against Samples 1–3 logic.
Implement complete stdin→stdout solution (cycle distances, feasibility, chain construction, LIS-based LCS, answer) in O(N log N).
Mentally edge-test: all zeros→0; balls only at X→0 (dist 0 yields empty chain); off-cycle ball→-1; identity perms with non-X ball→-1; overlapping chains use SCS; X never operated.

**Correctness of reduction**: Since P, Q are permutations, each color's graph is disjoint cycles; a ball reaches X iff it starts on X's cycle for its color's permutation. Operating the farthest ball's path to X (excluding X) in order automatically carries all nearer same-color balls, since they sit on that same cycle path and only move when their box is operated.

**Lower bound/achievability**: Any valid sequence must contain both chains as subsequences (each chain vertex must fire at least once, in order), and any common supersequence is achievable — at shared vertices both colors' balls have arrived before it fires, and balls of one color never sit on the other color's exclusive chain vertices. Hence min = |R| + |B| − LCS.
**Sample check**: Sample 1 → chains [2,1,4]/[5,1] (1-indexed), LCS 1 → 4 ✓; Sample 2 → 0 ✓; Sample 3 → red ball off X's cycle → -1 ✓; Sample 4 → 3+7−2 = 8 ✓.
**Edge cases**: balls only at X give dist 0 and empty chain (0 ops); `compute_dist` terminates since P,Q are permutations; LIS via `bisect_left` is strict and O(N log N), well within N ≤ 2×10⁵.
